# atc — Airflow Traffic Control

> A terminal control tower (TUI) for Apache Airflow 3 environments that sit behind
> awkward network paths: inside a private EKS/Kubernetes cluster, or in AWS MWAA with
> no public webserver. It keeps the connection path — which environment, reached by
> which mechanism, at what latency — on screen at all times, so you never trigger a DAG
> against the wrong environment. Python, built on Textual. MIT licensed.

## What problem it solves

- [Airflow behind a private network](README.md#what-you-get): Opening the Airflow web UI
  for a cluster-internal or VPC-private deployment normally means a manual
  `kubectl port-forward`, a bastion, or a VPN. atc owns one long-lived port-forward for
  the whole session and rebuilds it automatically if it dies.
- [MWAA without a public webserver](src/atc/core/providers/mwaa.py): Two auth strategies
  with automatic fallback — `mwaa:InvokeRestApi` (AWS proxies to the webserver
  server-side, no token exchange, 10s timeout, 6MB response cap), falling back to
  `CreateWebLoginToken` → `POST /pluginsv2/aws_mwaa/login` → session cookie. Credentials
  come from the normal AWS chain; the config file holds no secrets.
- [Triggering a DAG against the wrong environment](src/atc/tui/render.py): The
  always-visible connection bar renders `kind ▸ hops ▸ port  ● latency  vVERSION`, and
  read-only profiles are marked `⊘` on their tab before you look at them, not after you
  press the trigger key.
- [Airflow task failed with no logs (exit code -9, SIGKILL)](src/atc/core/providers/k8s.py):
  When Airflow returns an empty task log, that usually means the worker was killed before
  it could write. atc reports the empty log as a finding rather than showing a blank
  pane, and on Kubernetes falls back to reading the log file directly off the scheduler's
  log PVC via `kubectl exec`.
- [Monitoring hundreds of DAGs cheaply](src/atc/tui/app.py): The main screen is a
  starred watch list, not a full DAG list, so refresh cost is O(favourites) instead of
  one `dagRuns` call per DAG in the environment.
- [Switching between dev, staging and prod](src/atc/tui/app.py): One tab per configured
  environment, each with its own live connection, watch list and cursor. Tabs connect
  lazily — opening the app never dials every environment you have configured.

## Core modules

- [src/atc/core/provider.py](src/atc/core/provider.py): The eight-method `AirflowProvider`
  protocol and the shared `RestApiProvider` that speaks the Airflow 3 `/api/v2` REST API.
- [src/atc/core/providers/k8s.py](src/atc/core/providers/k8s.py): Long-lived
  `kubectl port-forward` with self-healing, admin password read from a cluster secret,
  exchanged for a JWT that is renewed 60s before its `exp` claim, plus the PVC log fallback.
- [src/atc/core/providers/mwaa.py](src/atc/core/providers/mwaa.py): MWAA auth strategy A/B
  with automatic selection, 12-hour web session caching and Airflow-version guarding.
- [src/atc/core/providers/fake.py](src/atc/core/providers/fake.py): Deterministic fake
  environment that drives `atc --fake` and the entire test suite.
- [src/atc/core/models.py](src/atc/core/models.py): Frozen dataclasses passed between
  providers and the UI — `ConnectionInfo`, `DagSummary`, `DagRun`, `TaskInstance`, `LogChunk`.
- [src/atc/tui/render.py](src/atc/tui/render.py): Pure formatting — run-history sparkline
  strips, state glyphs, duration and relative-time formatting, the connection bar.
- [src/atc/tui/app.py](src/atc/tui/app.py): Textual screens (watch list, runs, log) and
  the declarative keymap.
- [src/atc/wizard.py](src/atc/wizard.py), [src/atc/tui/wizard_app.py](src/atc/tui/wizard_app.py):
  `atc configure` — discovers kubectl contexts/namespaces, AWS profiles and MWAA
  environments, and writes `~/.config/atc/config.toml`.

## Scope and limits

- Airflow 3 only (`/api/v2`). An Airflow 2 environment is refused by name rather than
  failing obscurely.
- Read-mostly. The single write path is triggering a DAG, behind a confirmation, and it
  is refused outright on a profile marked `readonly = true`.
- Not a scheduler, not a deployment tool, not a replacement for the Airflow web UI's
  graph and Gantt views.
